How to use this volume
Part I. The finite quantum seed calculus develops the packet language and states the precise scope
of the archived formal proof.
Part II. The strengthened development extends this language through seventy-nine theorem,
proposition, lemma, and corollary proofs.
Part III. Six supplements give the detailed mathematical constructions behind the formal proofs,
followed by three alternative derivations.
Part IV. Forty worked visual pages connect the formulas to finite models and identify the hypothe-
ses needed at each continuum boundary.
Reading this edition
A seed is useful only together with the operators allowed to act on it. Paper VII follows that principle
through symmetry packets, quantum circuits, moving projectors, channels, effective dynamics, and
refinement. The finite calculus in Part I supplies the common language. The strengthened development
in Part II gives broader bounded constructions and limit criteria. Part III retains the detailed proof
completions rather than reducing them to a status summary.
The original finite item numbers keep the prefix I. The strengthened development has the prefix
II, and the supplementary constructions have the prefix III. All nine mathematical source parts are
retained. This edition revises their explanatory prose while preserving the mathematical expressions,
hypotheses, proof steps, and statement inventory. The accompanying report records the changes. Over-
lapping statements and proofs are retained because their hypotheses and uses differ. Their total is not
a count of independent discoveries.
The selected archived formal checkpoint covers nineteen scoped manuscript items. It records 323
explicit theorem declarations across twenty-five active Lean proof modules. These are different units.
The strengthened Part II is outside that nineteen-item contract. The formal evidence comes from the
archived checkpoint of 6 September 2026. The present prose revision does not report a fresh Lean
compilation. Exact hypotheses, declarations, inherited compiler records, and reproduction instructions
appear in the Lean companion.
Five explicitly named conjectures remain open in the finite core: anomaly-free refinement, uniform
Feshbach control, Lorentzian reconstruction, the Einstein infrared limit, and massless spin-two pack-
ets. Bounded direct limits and norm limits provide useful criteria. Each physical target still needs the
additional structure stated in its conjecture.
Four distinctions to keep in view
A seed’s algebraic orbit is different from a unitary state-preparation orbit. Compression is different
from an effective resolvent. A normalized channel is different from an unnormalized error family.
A finite spectrum is different from a continuum particle interpretation. Keeping these distinctions
visible makes the later results easier to use.
Read Part I first for the packet grammar and the finite statements. Turn to Part II for bounded operator
transport, spectral and channel constructions, and refinement towers. Use Part III when the geometric
bundle construction or a formal specialization needs more detail. The visual atlas follows the same
topics through explicit examples. It illustrates the statements with finite data and does not replace their
proofs.

I.15 Conclusion
The quantum realization of the seed calculus begins with a primitive state and a declared operator
grammar. Symmetry projectors resolve the state and every operator into exact packets. In these co-
ordinates, circuit products become sums over packet paths, and Hamiltonian symmetry appears as
a diagonal block structure. When that symmetry is broken, the resulting transfer is measured by the
leakage estimates.
Moving packets carry a canonical connection and curvature. Channels and measurements act on the
corresponding operator packets, while the conditions for error correction become statements about
compression to the code. Exact elimination retains the influence of hidden sectors through self-energy
and memory.
The finite theory therefore provides a coherent language for
seed reachability + symmetry resolution + circuit paths
+effective dynamics + geometric transport + constraint diagnostics
A physical continuum theorem remains open. The next required results are anomaly-free refinement,
uniform control of effective operators, Lorentzian reconstruction, the Einstein infrared limit, and a
positive massless spin-two sector. Each requires its own hypotheses and proof. Agreement in a finite
numerical model cannot replace those arguments.

II.15 Conclusion
A complete packet family gives one coordinate language for finite quantum structure. Group characters
produce symmetry packets. Charged operators obey exact selection rules. Circuits become coherent
sums over packet paths. The canonical moving connection separates geometric transport from physical
mixing. Density matrices and channels use two sided packets, while channel covariance becomes block
preservation on operator space and symmetry of the Choi matrix.
Compression to a code gives a natural error correction obstruction. Its vanishing is the Knill
Laflamme condition. Diagonalizing the resulting coefficient matrix produces orthogonal syndrome
packets and an exact recovery on the error span. Schur Feshbach elimination gives an equally exact
description of hidden Hamiltonian packets. Their frequency response is the self energy, and their time
response is a positive definite memory kernel.
Positive Euclidean transfer gives finite reflection positivity. Periodic lattice heat traces converge to the
continuum torus at every fixed positive diffusion time, and the continuum small time spectral dimen-
sion is recovered after the refinement limit. Constraint closure is measured by a quotient of operator
space, not by compression to the physical kernel.

Abstract
A packet operator is a linear map written between the members of a finite direct sum. We study the
resulting computational representation before choosing a processor or kernel. Exact formulas are given
for block sparse application, block diagonal plus low rank algebra, Woodbury inversion, support prop-
agation, block preconditioning, and packetwise perturbation. Products of low rank corrections ad-
mit optimal recompression through a small singular value problem, with explicit error propagation
through a product chain. A rooted candidate decomposition supports an exact compiler when repre-
sentation cost and error are additive. Dynamic programming gives the optimal Lagrangian pruning,
an exact quantized error budget algorithm, and a local update rule. Discrete precision assignment
becomes a multiple choice budget problem. Arithmetic, storage, data movement, launch count, discov-
ery, transfer, and materialization are kept as separate costs. A preserved corpus of 154 recorded CPU
and GPU measurements illustrates regular packet gains, precision frontiers, crossover behavior, and
retained negative controls. Its largest reported structured ratio is 14.89 against a device resident dense
GPU calculation, with archived matching-metadata limitations stated explicitly. The paper proves fi-
nite algebraic and optimization statements. Hardware measurements remain specific to their recorded
environment, and no generic dense matrix exponent or universal discovery algorithm is claimed.

quantities. The figures display the computed records. They do not report timings or identify actual hardware

1 Introduction
A matrix can look dense while its action is not. Independent diagonal blocks, sparse transfers, low rank
couplings, tensor factors, and transform coordinates can remove most of the arithmetic and storage
before a kernel is launched. The gain is mathematical first. A device can exploit only the structure that
the representation exposes.

The active addresses form a directed graph. Block dimensions, block types, approximation tolerances,
and output requirements turn this graph into a computational intermediate representation.
The underlying linear algebra is classical. Direct and iterative methods are treated in [14, 25, 9]. Low
rank approximation and updates are governed by singular value decomposition and the Sherman Mor-
rison Woodbury identity [11, 22, 15, 4]. Floating point analysis follows the standard model in [17, 20].
Randomized discovery of low rank structure is developed in [16, 21]. Communication and attainable
performance are shaped by data movement and arithmetic intensity [19, 27, 2, 12].
The first task is semantic. A compressed representation must specify the operator that it denotes. It
must also specify what an algorithm returns. A product represented by block and low rank factors is
not the same output as an explicit matrix. A timing comparison is valid only after the output contract
and timing scope agree.
The second task is algebraic. Block diagonal plus low rank operators are closed under multiplication
before recompression. Their unrecompressed rank grows additively. Woodbury inversion reduces a
large inverse to packet solves and one small dense inverse. The low rank factors can then be recom-
pressed by orthogonalizing them and taking the singular value decomposition of a small core. This
produces the best truncated approximation in spectral and Frobenius norm.
The third task is combinatorial. Sparse transfer graphs predict possible support under powers, poly-
nomials, and Schur elimination. A directed acyclic graph gives a finite path expansion. A block trian-
gular solve can be scheduled by topological level. Graph regularity matters because equal shapes can
be batched, while irregular edges require indexing and accumulation.
The fourth task is numerical. Packet perturbations can be certified by their block sensitivities. A con-
tinuous model assigns tolerances through a convex calculation. Upper bounds on available tolerances

The central computational result concerns compilation. Suppose a finite rooted tree records candi-
date refinements. Each node may be kept as one representation or split into its children. If cost and error
are additive across the selected leaves, the optimal pruning is found exactly by dynamic programming.
A quantized error budget has a second exact dynamic program. The decision is stable when the score
gap exceeds the perturbation in the local models. A change inside one subtree requires recomputa-
tion only along the ancestor chain. These results prove a restricted packet compiler. They do not solve
unrestricted discovery or arbitrary device scheduling.
The measured part uses a sanitized corpus collected on one recorded CPU and one NVIDIA GeForce
RTX 3070 Ti Laptop GPU. The preserved corpus contains 154 recorded rows from sixteen suites. The
timings are inherited observations; no GPU timing is rerun for this edition. Regular equal block opera-
tors and block diagonal plus low rank operators show large gains. Recursive HODLR, Strassen multipli-
cation, iterative refinement, a small Walsh Hadamard transform, and an attempted two stream overlap
provide negative controls. These rows are retained because structure does not guarantee speed.

and reuse count. The archived rows do not satisfy every field of this ideal contract: source-value hashes
and explicit correctness-reference fields are absent; setup, discovery, and reuse metadata are sparse.
Recorded ratios are consequently descriptive comparisons under their stated scopes, rather than full-
provenance fair matches.
The mathematical statements are finite. The empirical statements apply only to the recorded envi-
ronment and generated cases. The article does not claim a new generic matrix multiplication exponent.
Fast matrix multiplication and its stability form a separate theory [26, 10]. It also does not claim that
every structured matrix has a profitable GPU realization.

2.2 Output contracts
Definition 2.7 (Output contract). An output contract specifies the mathematical object returned
by an algorithm. The contract may require an explicit vector, an explicit matrix, block factors, low
rank factors, spectral factors, or an implicit operator with a declared application rule.
Definition 2.8 (Timing scope). A timing scope states which costs are included. Possible costs in-
clude structure discovery, compilation, host transfer, device transfer, kernel execution, graph cap-
ture, graph replay, factor reconstruction, and explicit materialization.
Proposition 2.9 (Contract conversion). Suppose one algorithm returns a compressed representation 𝑅and
another returns an explicit object 𝑌. A direct timing comparison is valid only if
decode(𝑅) = 𝑌
and the time required by decode is included, or if the downstream task consumes 𝑅directly.
Proof. Without decoding, the two procedures return different mathematical objects. A timing ratio be-
tween different outputs does not compare implementations of the same map. Including the decoding
cost gives two procedures with the same output. If the next operation consumes 𝑅, decoding is not
part of the declared computation.
Remark 2.10. A compressed product and an explicit matrix product may both be exact. They still have
different contracts. This distinction becomes decisive when materialization costs 𝑛2 entries.

9.4 Decision stability and local updates
Definition 9.10 (Decision gap). At an internal node 𝑣, let
𝑔𝑣= |𝐾𝜆(𝑣) −𝑆𝜆(𝑣)| .
This is the gap between the keep and split scores after the child subproblems have been solved.
Theorem 9.11 (Compiler stability). Suppose the solved keep score and split score at every internal node
change in absolute value by less than 𝑔𝑣/2. These are scores after child subproblems have been solved, rather
than unconstrained changes in raw local costs. Then every strict keep or split decision in the original optimal
pruning remains unchanged.
Proof. If the original keep score is lower by 𝑔𝑣, then after perturbation it can increase by less than 𝑔𝑣/2,
while the split score can decrease by less than 𝑔𝑣/2. The order remains strict. The split case is the same.
Apply the argument from the leaves upward.
Theorem 9.12 (Local recompilation). Suppose local costs change only inside the subtree rooted at 𝑢,
while ancestor and sibling local models are unchanged. Use correct cached sibling values from the old solve.
Then every dynamic programming value outside that subtree and outside the ancestor chain from 𝑢to the
root remains unchanged. Recomputing the subtree at 𝑢and that ancestor chain gives the exact new global
optimum.
Proof. A node value depends only on its own local data and the values of its children. Nodes outside
the changed subtree and outside the ancestor chain have the same local data and the same child values.
Their values remain unchanged. Every affected dependency lies inside the changed subtree or on the
unique path from 𝑢to the root.
Remark 9.13 (Boundary of the compiler theorem). The exact compiler requires a finite candidate tree
and additive local models. Arbitrary overlapping decompositions, nonlocal cache interactions, global
rank coupling, and unrestricted structure discovery can destroy optimal substructure. No universal
approximation factor is proved for those settings.
10 Device scheduling and amortization
10.1 Shape classes
Definition 10.1 (Shape class). Two active packet blocks lie in the same shape class when their
input dimension, output dimension, right hand side count, scalar type, accumulation type, and
kernel contract agree.
Proposition 10.2 (Launch reduction by shape). Suppose 𝐵independent active blocks fall into 𝑔shape classes,
and suppose the backend accepts one batched array or pointer list for each class. Grouped execution then requires
at most 𝑔launches instead of 𝐵, without changing the arithmetic or the output.
Proof. Place all blocks in one class along a batch dimension and invoke one batched kernel for that class.
Every block receives the same local computation. One launch per class is sufficient.
CUDA provides graph capture and replay for repeated dependency graphs [23]. These mechanisms
reduce repeated launch work, but they do not change the operator or its arithmetic count.
10.2 Critical path
Theorem 10.3 (Acyclic schedule depth). Let a packet task graph be acyclic. Assume every task takes
one normalized stage, every edge is a dependency, and an unlimited number of independent tasks may run
concurrently. For a nonempty finite graph, the minimum possible number of sequential stages equals the
number of vertices on a longest directed path. The empty task graph has depth zero.
Proof. Every path gives a lower bound because its tasks must execute in order. The topological level
schedule in theorem 6.5 achieves exactly this depth. With no tasks, the empty schedule has depth zero.

11 Benchmark contracts and measurement protocol
Performance data are meaningful only after the mathematical and timing contracts are fixed. The pro-
tocol follows standard concerns from numerical linear algebra, floating point analysis, and machine
performance modeling [17, 14, 27].
Definition 11.1 (Case signature). A case signature records the dimensions, packet layout, rank,
right hand side count, random seed, source values, source type, reference computation, and output
contract.
Definition 11.2 (Fair match). Two measured rows are a fair match when they share one case sig-
nature, return the same declared output, use the same correctness reference, and have identical
timing scopes. If one row includes an extra conversion or setup cost, it is a different scope and
must be reported separately or added to both rows before comparison.
Proposition 11.3 (Fair matching is an equivalence relation). On rows with complete metadata, equality of
the case signature, output contract, correctness reference, and timing scope is an equivalence relation.
Proof. Equality of each metadata field is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. Their conjunction has the
same properties.
Definition 11.4 (Representation gain). Representation gain compares dense and structured work
or storage for the same operator, independently of the processor.
Definition 11.5 (Device gain). Device gain compares processors for the same representation, out-
put, and timing scope.

14 Hardware implications and exact boundaries
The finite results suggest a device interface with grouped block kernels, low rank contractions, packet
metadata, a transfer graph scheduler, and per edge precision tags. Such an interface may reduce ma-
terialization and repeated launch work when the operator family remains closed under the chosen
representation.
The exact results stop at a finite candidate tree and a declared device model. Three broader problems
remain open.
1. A universal discovery algorithm would need to find a profitable packet structure from an arbi-
trary operator and data distribution. The simultaneous spectral theorem and randomized low
rank approximation cover special cases only.
2. A universal compiler would need a controlled approximation factor when costs are nonlocal and
candidate decompositions overlap. The dynamic programs in theorems 9.4 and 9.8 do not cover
that setting.

15 Conclusion
A packet operator representation records which block maps exist, how they are stored, and what output
they denote. Exact block evaluation and composition turn the support graph into algebra. Arithmetic,
storage, and one pass data movement follow from the active block dimensions. Block diagonal plus low
rank operators remain closed under multiplication before recompression. Their inverse is reduced by
Woodbury, and their correction can be recompressed optimally through a small singular value prob-
lem.
Sparse transfer graphs predict path support, triangular schedule depth, and possible fill under elimi-
nation. Packet diagonal structure gives local Krylov spaces and a certified block Jacobi condition bound.

F.7 Regressions, reproduction and claim boundary
Exact mathematical guarantees versus numerical implementations
Independent numerical checks. A deterministic NumPy complex128 mirror tested 182 input-factor
pairs at 638 truncation cases. The cases include rectangular matrices, rank-deficient and zero factors,
empty spaces, repeated singular values, rank zero and ranks beyond the core width. Comparison used
both the small core and an independently computed ambient SVD reference. There were 3,190 arbitrary
rank-bounded competitors, nine invalid-input rejection controls and two checks demonstrating failure
when essential assumptions are removed.
The largest relative tail/reconstruction discrepancy was below 3.7×10−15, against a declared 2×10−9
tolerance. The mirror uses numerical rank thresholds and a numerical SVD to construct column bases.
It is not compiled or extracted Lean code, a proof for all inputs, or a GPU benchmark. The formal result
uses exact ranks and exact factorization equations.
Reproduce from the extracted source root.
python3 scripts/verify_integrity.py

The unit tests and numerical mirror require NumPy. The Lean verification path needs Python 3.10 or

The runner also supports bounded batches with --max-checks and hash-checked --resume. A partial
checkpoint is not a pass.
What is complete. The 56-item manuscript-proved register is covered under the recorded hypotheses.
The original theorem says to take orthonormal factors and a core SVD. The new construction and proof
discharge the recompression conclusion from those exact factorization equations. In particular, no best-
approximation assertion or error formula is hidden in an input certificate.
What is not claimed. General SVD existence or a numerical SVD implementation is not newly for-
malized. The four classical entries remain separately tracked; the ordered-SVD-data optimality argu-
ment now has checked support, while the CG algorithm theorem, floating-point product model and
simultaneous-decomposition input are not newly proved in full. No new generic matrix-multiplication
exponent, floating-point stability theorem or hardware speedup follows from this release.
The original manuscript, bibliography, source package and all five earlier supplements are preserved.
Historical CPU/GPU measurements, earlier compiler execution suites and Papers I–VII in full were not
rerun. Prose-to-formal correspondence is an explicit mathematical review, not an automated theorem
equating a sentence with a Lean type.

it need not preserve every optimum of the unquantized problem.
Why the complexity is pseudo polynomial
For a declared integer budget 𝐵, a table has 𝐵+ 1 possible exact-weight states. A direct merge checks
at most (𝐵+ 1)2 state pairs. At 𝐵= 255, this means 256 states and 65,536 candidate pairs at a merge, even
though the budget fits in eight binary digits.
With a bounded number of children, the paper’s direct tree implementation therefore has quadratic
budget dependence at each node. Polynomial dependence on the numerical value of 𝐵does not mean poly-
nomial dependence on the binary input length. These are counts of declared states and pairs, not measured
runtimes or claims that every state is reachable.
Read this as: The dynamic program is exact for its integer data. Conservative conversion and the
numerical size of the budget are separate obligations that determine its accuracy and practical scale.

Abstract
We prove Nishibuchi’s generalized Euler congruence conjecture in its full stated parameter range
and develop sharper arithmetic consequences. For every prime-power packet width, a charged
Hurwitz differential operator transfers integral difference estimates through the reciprocal generating
series. In the dyadic case this gives mixed finite-difference bounds at every row, without a starting
threshold. For the four addresses of width four, a divided-power argument adds the factorial
gain v2(k!), determines every repeated-step valuation in addresses zero and one, and gives a
stronger address-two estimate with exact values at all power-of-two orders. The corresponding first
differences yield least periods and bijective isometric continuations onto explicit dyadic residue
classes. We also determine exact Taylor radii for three addresses. The manuscript retains the complete
earlier arithmetic, lifting, deformation, and analytic-regularity development, with dated historical
appendices. A separate appendix states the precise remaining simplicity problem for ordinary
Euler tails. Formal coverage is explicit: the external conjecture and several four-address results
have inherited Lean verification; the new factorial, mixed-step, all-rank, and radius arguments are
written proofs with recorded audits and exact computational checks, and await dedicated Lean
formalization.

1 Scope and conventions
The central objects are sequences and polynomial equations equipped with arithmetic coordinates.
Residue projectors select addresses in a sequence, finite differences measure compatibility between
nearby addresses, and valuation bounds control the passage from finite precision to a p-adic limit.
These constructions provide a common language for the Euler packet results and the later lifting results.
Each theorem nevertheless retains its own coefficient ring, topology and nonsingularity hypotheses.
This edition integrates the original arithmetic framework with the completed extensions. The stated
external Nishibuchi conjecture is proved in its full specified parameter range. The dyadic refinements
and polynomial deformation theorems give stronger conclusions under the hypotheses stated with
each result. The native conjectures retain their original identifiers, 13.2 and 13.3, when discussed as
research questions, although the section numbering of this consolidated manuscript is new.
Throughout, N = {0, 1, 2, . . .}. When p is prime, Zp denotes the p-adic integers and Qp their fraction
field. We normalize vp(p) = 1. For a rational or p-adic quantity, a displayed lower valuation bound
is understood with the mathematical convention vp(0) = +∞. The corresponding formal predicates
are zero-safe: the quantity is zero or its valuation meets the stated bound. An exact finite valuation
assertion requires a nonzero quantity, and this is stated where used. Congruence in Zp means ideal

2 Arithmetic packets and coefficient transport
We work with sequences, formal power series, and finite recurrence states. Residue selectors isolate
coefficients in a chosen congruence class, while triangular transport expresses the same object in new
coordinates. A valuation filtration determines how many coordinates are needed at a given precision.
Together, these operations provide a common framework for the Euler congruences and the finite
lifting constructions developed later.
The original arithmetic seed notation
S = (A, a0, O, R, {PN,j}, w, τp)
records a coefficient ring or module, a seed, allowed operators, relations, residue selectors, a depth
weight, and a topology. This notation describes the ingredients of the construction; a category of seed
presentations and a notion of equivalence still require separate definitions. We therefore state each
theorem for a concrete object. Section 12 discusses the additional structure needed for the original
native conjectures.
The Lean declarations cited in this section have namespace prefix KomorebiPaperIX. Their exact
modules and source hashes are recorded in the accompanying statement map. All belong to the
preserved baseline formalization; this section brings their statements and proofs together.

9.1 Proof coverage and remaining questions
The results in these sections are mathematical theorems with detailed proofs and preserved audit
evidence. Their formal status must be read statement by statement. The recovered Paper IX release
already contains Lean results for the rank-four threshold-free homogeneous bound, the sharp first-
difference laws, the least periods, and the dyadic isometry and image conclusions. Those inherited
results should not be described as missing merely because the earlier short completion supplement did
not include their later modules.
The all-rank dyadic and general prime-power transfer proof presented here, the factorial improve-
ments, the mixed leading-parity classification, the Bernoulli power-order sharpness, the all-rank lower-
half exact laws, the complete rank-eight extension, and the exact Taylor-radius arguments have not
received new Lean formalization in this strengthening. A mathematical audit and an exact computation
are neither a Lean compilation nor external peer review. The separate Lean guide records the recovered
formal declarations and any fresh release checks without extending their coverage to these new claims.
The completed external statement is Nishibuchi’s Conjecture 3.9 in its prescribed parameter family
and coefficient normalization. These stronger congruences enlarge its dyadic branch and remove its
starting threshold there. They do not settle every Euler problem. In particular, the following questions
remain separate:
• a complete exact higher-difference law at all non-power-of-two orders in address two;
• complete higher-difference valuations and the exact ordinary Taylor radius in address three;
• a classification of the upper-half dyadic addresses having an exact first-difference metric law at
arbitrary larger ranks;
• the distinct universal simplicity or nonvanishing question for the later Euler-tail residuals, and
the original native Paper IX conjectures beyond the completed external statement.
The exact counterexamples above rule out the naive universal upper-half isometry, and mixed cancella-
tions rule out unconditional baseline sharpness for arbitrary stencils. No global historical-priority or
novelty assertion is made for these strengthened statements.

12 Open questions and further directions
The arithmetic results above resolve Nishibuchi’s conjecture throughout its stated parameter range. The
local analyticity and differentiability theorem is also complete under its stated invertibility hypothesis.
What remains is a set of extensions and sharper classifications, together with the broader questions
raised by the original native seed-calculus program.
12.1 Singular persistence beyond an invertible solved block
The weighted lifting theorem allows the solved Jacobian to be noninvertible modulo p provided that
it is invertible over Qp with a controlled inverse. This includes a substantial class of lifts often called
singular modulo p. The next problem is to understand Jacobians that remain rank-deficient over Qp,
where the inverse construction is no longer available.
For a fixed polynomial system F ∈Z[X1, . . . , Xd]e, a precision L ≥1, and a root ¯x modulo pL, let
LF,L( ¯x) = {x′ ∈(Z/pL+1Z)d : F(x′) = 0, x′ ≡¯x
(mod pL)}.
The finite obstruction theorem decides whether this set is empty from the residual digit and reduced
Jacobian. When it is nonempty, the theorem also determines its cardinality and affine kernel structure.
The conclusion concerns one level: vanishing of the obstruction permits the next step, but does not
guarantee that subsequent steps are possible.
For example, X2 −5 has the root 1 modulo 2, and both 1 and 3 lift it to roots modulo 4. Every odd
square is 1 modulo 8, so neither branch continues to a root modulo 8. Thus even a successful first
correction can lead to branches that stop at the following level.
We seek structural hypotheses and higher obstruction data that control an entire singular branch,
including its behavior under coefficient and parameter deformation. One route is to propagate suitable
conditions from level to level. Another is to prove existence at all levels in a form that yields compatible
branches. The finite obstruction calculus supplies the tests for individual levels, but a persistence
theorem needs a further argument linking them. Any general formulation must allow multiple branches,
later obstructions, and changes in the rank of the Jacobian.

and edges given by R.
The component maps fR : A →CR and gR : B →CR have the following universal property. For
every set Y and maps h : A →Y, k : B →Y satisfying h(a) = k(b) whenever R(a, b), there is a unique
map u : CR →Y with u ◦fR = h and u ◦gR = k.
Proof. Any equality representation is rectangular, since the three assumed equalities imply f (a) =
g(b) = f (a′) = g(b′).
Conversely, suppose R is rectangular. An edge always gives equal component labels. If a ∈A and
b ∈B have equal component labels, there is a finite path between them. Its length is odd. A path of
length one is already an R-edge. A longer path begins with three edges a −b1 −a1 −b2. Rectangularity
gives the edge a −b2. Replacing these three edges by that edge shortens the path by two. Induction
therefore yields R(a, b). This proves the exact equality representation. Finiteness follows because the
component set is a quotient of the finite set A ⊔B.
For the universal property, combine h and k into a function on A ⊔B. It is constant across every
edge by hypothesis, hence along every finite path. It therefore descends to a well-defined function on
components. The two required factorization identities hold by construction. They determine the value
on every component, proving uniqueness. □
For example, the three pairs (a0, b0), (a1, b0), (a1, b1) without (a0, b1) fail rectangularity. Every equality-
label representation agreeing on those three pairs also admits the fourth pair, so it cannot represent that
relation exactly.

prove rectangularity. The universal property holds for the component quotient even when rectangularity
fails, but then the equality locus strictly enlarges R. The theorem establishes neither a minimum number
of labels nor a smallest spine in the manuscript’s unspecified category. It carries no automatic topology,
spectral information or Frobenius compatibility. Evidence: prose proof in this note, not a Lean
formalization.

D.12 Conclusion
The local arithmetic theory now has one common architecture. The finite character coordinate identifies
the torsion phase. The source and kernel product reconstructs the Euler coefficient. The kernel valuation
records certified precision. Carmichael and Mahler coordinates describe the remaining principal unit
motion. Polyphase analysis resolves additional local digits, records carries and shifts exactly, and
transports Mahler coefficients through a finite affine kernel.
The odd and dyadic cases agree at the level of convolution and differ at the level of integral geometry.
At odd primes the source must be depleted before it becomes a unit mode interpolation. At the dyadic
prime the source extends directly to an analytic integral function. The dyadic kernel has exact weight
4r −1, giving the optimal uniform modulus 24M+3 after depth M.
Three tasks remain outside the proved region. The first is a complete finite difference estimate after
the congruential triangular inverse. The second is an exact higher valuation theory for the affine Mahler
kernel. The third is a global existence theorem for local systems that do not already arise from one
integral source.

The principal statements are universal over their explicit inputs, not finite numerical observations.
The main mathematical connection
A sampled state uk = vNk+j evolves by the actual jump matrix CN. Its recurrence is derived from the
characteristic polynomial of that matrix. No scalar recurrence or spectral decomposition is supplied as
a substitute for the desired conclusion.
For Fibonacci numbers, the state is independently defined from Mathlib’s actual sequence. The Lucas
sequence is independently defined by its initial values and recurrence. The trace and determinant of
CN are then proved to supply the sampled recurrence coefficients.
Important qualification
A d-dimensional state system supplies a recurrence of order at most d. Its minimal recurrence need
not have order d. The original statement is read as the characteristic-polynomial recurrence, not a
minimal-order claim. The formal equations also handle singular matrices, zero-dimensional spaces and
zero step.

packets are the special case N > 0 and 0 ≤j < N. The formula also permits offsets beyond that

Abstract
A residual representation is a genuine zeroth-order coordinate. All positive-depth perturbations
above it may fill its formal deformation neighborhood, but they cannot move into a different
residual class. This paper develops the corresponding universal object: a residual forest whose
roots are residual representations, whose finite levels are lifts modulo powers of a uniformizer, and
whose infinite branches are complete characteristic-zero objects. We prove the residual partition, no-
crossing, inverse-limit reconstruction, finite-branch compactness, exact smooth and singular branch
counts, packet decomposition of tangent and obstruction cohomology, a directed minimum-seed
theorem, rational seed-zeta formulas, and finite companion-forest completion. The coefficient prime
two is represented by a weighted forest in which characteristic-zero packets may merge modulo two
and become visible only at later depth. We then define a prime-independent system seed through
a common Frobenius spine, prove a compatible-carrier summand theorem under finite Frobenius
separation, and reduce finite occupancy in a fixed semisimple carrier to the nonnegative integer
trace of an exact joint projector. The paper does not prove that every admissible residual companion
exists or that every finite Hecke packet is occupied. Those two existence statements remain the exact
horizontal boundary beyond vertical deformation theory.

7 Residual transport categories
Vertical lifting never changes a residual root. Horizontal coverage requires operations whose residual
effect is not congruent to the identity. Examples that may define such transports include twisting,
duality, restriction, induction, tensor product, symmetric powers, exterior powers, and functorial
transfer. The word “may” is essential: each operation must preserve the deformation conditions and
the realization statement being transported.
Definition 7.1 (Admissible residual transport). An admissible transport from ¯ρ to ¯ρ′ consists of

for every coefficient algebra A, compatible with base change and reduction. When the transport is
reversible, it is an isomorphism in the residual transport groupoid. One-way operations give a directed
category.
For a finite collection of roots, record a directed edge u →v whenever occupancy or the relevant
property is known to propagate from u to v.
Definition 7.2 (Directed seed rank). For a directed transport graph G, define
srankG = min{|S| : ClG(S) = V(G)},
where ClG(S) is the set of vertices reachable from S.
Theorem 7.3 (Directed minimum-seed theorem). Let G be a finite directed graph. Collapse every strongly
connected component to one vertex, obtaining the condensation DAG. Then
srankG = #{source strongly connected components of G}.
One representative from each source component is a minimum seed set.
Proof. Every vertex of a finite DAG is reachable from a source, so one seed in each source component
reaches the entire condensation graph. Within a strongly connected component, one vertex reaches
every other. Hence the source representatives are sufficient.
Conversely, a source component has no incoming edge from another component. It cannot be reached
from a seed outside itself, so every generating seed set must meet it. Therefore the number of source
components is also a lower bound.
For reversible transports the condensation has one vertex per connected component, recovering the
undirected minimum-seed theorem.
Formal scope and propagation.
Reachability is the reflexive-transitive closure of the supplied directed
edge relation, and a strongly connected component is the actual quotient by mutual reachability. The
minimum seed count is defined independently as the least cardinality of a set that reaches all vertices.
Every covering set must meet every source component; conversely, meeting every source component
suffices in a finite graph. Thus any choice of one representative from each source is optimal. Empty
graphs have rank zero, and self-loops are permitted. Adding admissible edges cannot increase the
minimum seed count.
If a property P propagates along every supplied edge and holds at all selected seeds, it holds at every
reached vertex. These are explicit hypotheses. The minimum-seed theorem does not construct valid
arithmetic edges or supply initial occupancy.
Why the finite hypothesis cannot be dropped.
Take vertices {∗} ⊔{vn : n ∈N}, with ∗isolated and
edges vn+1 →vn. Every strongly connected component is a singleton, and {∗} is the unique source
component. No finite seed set covers all vertices: it can reach only indices no larger than the largest
chosen index. Both the unique-source statement and the failure of every finite cover are checked in
Lean. Hence one source component in an infinite condensation does not imply that one seed reaches all
objects.

11 A conditional system-completion criterion
The preceding results can be assembled without promoting their missing hypotheses to theorems.
Theorem 11.1 (Residual-system completion criterion). Fix an admissible arithmetic class. Suppose:
1. every object has a unique residual root in an exhaustive residual moduli space;
2. a common algebraic spine is defined for the desired system;
3. every coefficient-prime residual companion exists;
4. every companion forest has nonempty finite levels, finite branching, and inverse-limit closed local conditions;
5. the required horizontal transports preserve the common spine and the selected local deformation conditions.

compatible carrier, the summand is recovered at every coefficient prime by finitely many Frobenius traces.

hypothesis identifies any roots that are meant to be generated horizontally without changing the
prescribed spine. The final assertion is the compatible-carrier summand theorem.

15 Conclusion
The residual seed theory becomes precise once vertical and horizontal generation are separated. Positive-
depth perturbations can be complete within one formal component. They cannot change the residual
root. The universal arithmetic seed is therefore a forest rather than one branch:
residual roots −→finite deformation levels −→inverse-limit branches.
Projectors add three useful structures to this forest. They split tangent and obstruction complexes into
exact subproblems, they measure delayed dyadic visibility through weights, and they turn finite carrier
occupancy into an integer trace. Directed transport adds a fourth: it converts the informal question
“how many seeds are needed?” into the source-component count of a condensation graph.
The system-level boundary is now narrow enough to state without ambiguity. One must construct a
common algebraic spine, populate every residual companion forest, lift those companions through all
depths, and prove positive occupancy of the required global packets. The present paper proves the
formal reconstruction, counting, transport, compactness, carrier, and finite-projector theorems used in
that reduction. It does not assert the missing universal existence statements.

D.2 Why the assembly closes
The final proof is a conjunction. The first branch applies the checked inverse-limit-closed horizontal
completion theorem to the completed source family. The second branch constructs the finite arithmetic
separator and applies the checked compatible-carrier closure theorem. Claim 9.1 constructs its separator
independently of the carrier recovery. Claim 9.2 accepts the separator and the compatible-carrier packet.
The final source composes these results; it does not use its conclusion to establish either premise.
The two branches do not identify the recovered carrier’s supplied local Weil or period structures with
restrictions of the transported target family. They remain logically distinct outputs. A simultaneous
all-place carrier statement is obtained by applying the pointwise result at every place when the
corresponding carrier presentations are supplied.

Zero multiplicities are permitted by the formal endpoint. A nonzero occupied conclusion additionally
requires the manuscript’s declared nonzero-multiplicity premise and nonzero constituents. The module-
support/Fitting-ideal alternative is logically separate: its checked support formalization is inherited
and is not re-proved by this final module. No unrestricted companion existence, automorphy, carrier
existence, or universal p-adic Hodge comparison follows from this conditional assembly.

Abstract. Let K be a nonarchimedean local field. We resolve several finite layers that occur inside the local
Langlands correspondence for general linear groups. Frobenius semisimple Weil Deligne parameters first
split into irreducible Weil atoms and finite monodromy chains. In the tame case, character projectors show
that every irreducible atom is one transitive Frobenius orbit, and Mackey theory gives an exact greatest
common divisor and least common multiple rule for tensor packets. Regular finite field characters produce
primitive cuspidal projectors and finite Gauss phases. For wild data, projective intertwiners recover an
alternating commutator form. Its radical free quotient determines a finite Heisenberg representation, and
maximal isotropic averaging gives an exact selector. We prove a restricted one break bridge: an equivariant
symplectic isometry between a declared Galois envelope and a type side quotient induces the Heisenberg
comparison uniquely up to scalar, while one cyclic phase condition removes the remaining ambiguity. Odd
residue characteristic is governed by finite Weil phases. Residue characteristic two requires a quadratic
refinement and its Arf invariant. A matrix holonomy theorem then gives the exact gluing criterion on
a finite transport graph. The general arithmetic packet realization is stated as Conjecture 66. Detailed
ordinary proofs give restricted arithmetic realizations in all odd prime-power ranks and in all dyadic
ranks for the stated increasing-break families. The complete comparison of pair local factors remains a
conditional input for the same arithmetic candidate.

1 Introduction
The local Langlands correspondence for GLn(K) is an established theorem. It matches irreducible
smooth representations of GLn(K) with Frobenius semisimple Weil Deligne representations of
dimension n. Its proof and normalization draw on global methods, harmonic analysis, types, local
factors, and the geometry of Shimura varieties [19, 17, 8]. The present article asks a narrower structural
question. Which parts of the local correspondence admit finite packet coordinates whose projectors,
transfers, phases, and gluing laws can be proved directly?
The answer has a sharp division. The tame layers are explicit. A tame irreducible Weil representation
is induced from a character of an unramified extension. Its inertia restriction is one Frobenius orbit.
Regular characters of elliptic finite field tori give cuspidal blocks through the Deligne and Lusztig
construction [13]. Their tensor products are controlled by a greatest common divisor and least common
multiple decomposition. The corresponding cycle orientation and finite Gauss phases can be computed
exactly. These features are closely related to the tame lifting and essentially tame correspondence of
Bushnell and Henniart [4, 5, 6, 7, 9].
Wild data are different. The restriction to wild inertia need not split into cyclic characters. On the
type side, simple character theory produces finite symplectic quotients and Heisenberg representations
[11]. Canonical beta extensions fix a phase ambiguity in the extension to the normalizer [2, 14]. On the
Galois side, higher ramification gives a canonical filtration and strong numerical constraints [10]. The
missing construction is not another finite matrix calculation. It is a choice free passage from an arbitrary
wild inertia atom to a finite symplectic envelope that agrees with the type side quotient.
We therefore separate three levels of assertion. First, the article proves finite algebraic theorems
about tame orbits, Heisenberg groups, twisted group algebras, finite Weil phases, and transport graphs.
Second, it proves a restricted one break bridge once a normal wild datum and an equivariant symplectic
identification are declared. Third, it records the exact additional input needed to pass from that
restricted bridge to an independent construction of all wild atoms.
The finite Heisenberg theory used here is classical. We use the Stone von Neumann theorem, finite
Weil representations, and standard projective representation theory [15, 25, 26, 22, 16]. The contribution
is the way these results are arranged into one comparison diagram and the matrix holonomy theorem
that controls finite gluing. In residue characteristic two, the alternating form does not determine the
phase. A quadratic refinement and its Arf invariant are required. The underlying quadratic form theory
is standard [24].
Local factors provide the final test. Henniart showed that pair epsilon factors characterize the local
correspondence in the required range [18]. The tame packet calculations below recover exact local
polynomials and finite Gauss phases for the declared tame atoms. They do not supply the complete
pair factor comparison for arbitrary wild atoms. This boundary is retained throughout the paper.
This reading edition separates the missing arithmetic realization from the conditional identification
of one actual candidate. The endpoint formerly listed as proof obligation 66 (historical Theorem 16.2,
row 95 of the all-records register) is now conjecture 66. The finite theorem statements and proofs include
the geometric-Frobenius convention correction and the additional local corrections recorded in this
edition’s reading guide. The later restricted constructions are developed in section 19 and the detailed
construction appendices. Their evidence is ordinary proof with retained internal reviews, rather than
new Lean certificates. These reviews are not external peer review.

16 Local factor tests and the remaining bridge
Local class field theory identifies one dimensional Weil characters with characters of K× [27, 29].
The tame induction theorem extends this explicit picture to higher dimensional tame atoms. The
local polynomial and conductor calculations in propositions 5.4 and 5.8 therefore give explicit finite
invariants for the declared tame packets. Finite Gauss sums give the residue field phase. The full local
factor, however, also includes ramification depth, Haar measure normalization, the additive character
conductor, and wild interaction data.
Proposition 16.1 (Finite tame comparison package). For a tame induced atom, the following data are
determined by its packet coordinates:
(1) the dimension and inertia orbit
(2) the Frobenius cycle polynomial
(3) the Artin conductor
(4) the local polynomial
(5) the tensor refinement into interaction packets
(6) the finite Gauss sum of each declared residue character, with unit-modulus phase normalization when
that character is nontrivial.
Proof. The dimension and orbit follow from theorem 3.2. The cycle polynomial is proposition 4.4. For
rank greater than one, the conductor is proposition 5.8. In rank one, the Swan conductor is zero, and the
Artin conductor is zero for trivial inertia and one otherwise, by the formula Art = dim V −dim VIK +
Sw. The local polynomial is proposition 5.4. Tensor refinement is theorem 5.1. The Gauss sum is its
defining finite sum; for a nontrivial multiplicative character its unit phase is definition 6.2. For the
trivial character and a nontrivial additive character ψ, the sum is G(1, ψ) = −1, because the sum of ψ
over the whole field is zero.
□

18 Scope of the finite reconstruction
The article proves the following statements under their displayed hypotheses.
(1) Tame irreducible Weil atoms are transitive Frobenius packets induced from unramified
extensions.
(2) Regular tame packets have the stated Möbius count.
(3) Finite cuspidal blocks have exact primitive central projectors.
(4) Tame tensor products satisfy the greatest common divisor and least common multiple packet
formula.
(5) Tame local polynomials, conductors, and finite Gauss phases are explicit.
(6) Nondegenerate scalar projective commutators give full matrix twisted group algebras and
unique finite Heisenberg representations.
(7) A declared one break Clifford datum has a choice independent radical free symplectic envelope.
(8) An equivariant symplectic isometry gives a Heisenberg bridge unique up to scalar.
(9) One generator phase removes the scalar discrepancy for a cyclic stabilizer.
(10) Odd finite Weil phases and dyadic Arf signs are multiplicative across orthogonal break packets.
(11) Matrix holonomy on a fundamental cycle basis is the exact finite gluing obstruction.
The article does not independently prove the local Langlands correspondence, simple character
theory, the canonical beta extension, or universal wild companion existence. It does not construct the
Galois to type symplectic isometry for an arbitrary wild atom. It does not compare all pair local factors
in the wild case.

D.1 The useful simplification
Full critical-profile rigidity is unnecessary for the trivial-stabilizer finite attachment contract. An even
leading level produces a symplectic subspace that survives every later simple approximation. For the
independent rank-p Heisenberg tensor sources, this single subspace already has enough dimension to
hold every source plane, however many there are.
The argument below concerns the actual type in the source-defined arithmetic candidate. It does not
identify that type with a separately guessed binder parameter.
D.2 1. Leading-layer theorem
Let F have residue field k of cardinality q and residue characteristic p. Let pi be an actual irreducible
supercuspidal representation of GL_n(F) with torsion number one, where n=p^r. Suppose
a(pi)=n+N,
N>0 even,
v_p(N)=r−1.
Then an actual maximal simple type in pi, with Heisenberg quotient W = J1/H1, contains a
nondegenerate symplectic F_p-subspace S of dimension
[k:F_p] (p−1)p^(r−1).
For k=F_p this is exactly (p−1)p^(r−1). The subspace is the image of the concrete congruence group
U^(N/2)(A) in J1/H1. It is present regardless of the later critical exponents, their parities, or the number
of intermediate approximation fields.
D.2.1 1.1. Actual parameter field and leading level
By BK maximal-type existence, pi contains a maximal simple type. Its positive level follows from
a(pi)>n. Write its stratum as [A,N_A,0,beta], with parameter field K=F[beta]. BK 6.2.5 gives
t(pi)=n/e(K/F).
Thus e(K/F)=n. Since [K:F] divides n, K/F is totally ramified of degree n and has residue degree
one. The principal-order assertion after BK 6.2.5 gives e(A)=n. Accordingly A is the complete principal
hereditary order. The established conductor formula
a(pi)=n+n N_A/e(A)
now implies N_A=N. This is the same source-checked formula used in Block165, originating in
BH1999 Section 6.1 Lemma 2 and retained in PRINCIPAL_ORDER_CONDUCTOR161.md.
Put P=rad(A), Ua(A) = 1 + Pa for a>=1, and m=N/2.
D.2.2 1.2. The terminal minimal approximation has degree p
Apply the defining-sequence construction BK 2.4.1–2 to beta. Write gamma for its terminal minimal
approximation. Every transition has a critical level c<N, and gamma has the same A-level N as beta.
All approximation residue degrees divide f(K/F)=1, and all approximation ramification degrees divide
n. Therefore E=F[gamma] is totally ramified of degree d dividing n.
The scalar case is impossible: a scalar of F has A-valuation divisible by n, whereas v_p(N)=r−1. Thus
gamma is noncentral and minimal in the ordinary field sense. Its field valuation is
−v_E(gamma)=Nd/n.
Minimality, by BK 1.4.14–15, requires gcd(Nd/n,d)=1. Since d is a p-power and v_p(N)=r−1,
integrality first gives p|d, while coprimality forces d=p. Hence E/F is totally ramified of degree p.

n/p over E. Each P-grade has k-dimension n and each Q-grade has k-dimension n/p. In particular,
dim_k P^m/(Q^m+P^(m+1))=n−n/p.

approximation field in the defining sequence.

The minimal definitions BK 3.1.7–8 give

a>=floor(c_i/2)+1.

H^m(beta)=H^m(gamma).

= U^m(A)/H^m(gamma)
≅P^m/(Q^m+P^(m+1)).

E Actual scalar inertia phases and finite-cover descent
Evidence: ordinary proof using rank-one reciprocity, the given central character, and elementary
finite group arguments. The result constructs actual central matrix operators through a finite cover
and proves their descent. It does not construct a new arithmetic candidate or alter a canonical beta
extension.
E.1 1. Exact statement
Let F be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field k of cardinality q and residue characteristic
p. Put Q=q-1 and n=p^r, allowing r=0. Let rho:W_F -> GL_n(C) be a smooth Weil representation with
finite inertia image. Use the fixed reciprocity convention identifying its determinant with a character
omega:F× -> C×.
Let C be a finite group of order prime to p, and suppose its prescribed operators on the full source
carrier are
Omega_src(c)=chi(c)I_n,
where chi is a character and each Omega_src(c) belongs to the actual matrix image rho(I_F). A finite
cyclic scalar tame image is the intended example. This hypothesis refers to actual source operators, not
freely chosen phases on an unrelated multiplicity-space factor.
Let Pi be any already constructed irreducible smooth GL_n(F) representation with central character
omega. Suppose it has its supplied actual inducing representation Lambda on N, with F× contained in
N, and an attached finite sector E=eLambda realizing the prescribed source Heisenberg packet. Assume
the prescribed C action on the source scalar extension is trivial, and that the honest scalar phase on the
packet is the same chi above.
Theorem. There is a finite group C_tilde surjecting onto C and a genuine homomorphism
g:C_tilde -> F× I_n contained in N
whose action on Lambda and on Pi descends to the prescribed honest C action chi(c)I. Every finite
sector is stable under this action. Any center-preserving Heisenberg attachment and its intertwiner
are C-equivariant. The retained sector-induction recovery maps recover the same Lambda and
Pi equivariantly. All actual inducing data, including the fixed canonical beta extension, remain
unchanged.
The arithmetic action is supplied by actual central matrices, with an explicit finite-cover descent. The
theorem does not assert that C itself embeds as a matrix subgroup. Such an embedding can fail even
for a genuine scalar tame source, as Section4 shows.
E.2 2. Construction and proof
Let D=k×, and let Teich:D -> O_F× be the canonical multiplicative lift. For p=2 this is still the prime-to-p
root-of-unity subgroup. When q=2, D is trivial and the argument below forces chi trivial as well.
Local reciprocity identifies the determinant image of inertia with
det rho(I_F)=omega(O_F×).
The unit group decomposes as
O_F× = Teich(D) times U_F¹.
The smooth character image omega(U_F¹) is a finite p-group, while omega(Teich(D)) has order prime
to p. Therefore the prime-to-p elements of omega(O_F×) are exactly omega(Teich(D)).
For every c in C, the actual-source hypothesis implies
chi(c)^n=det(Omega_src(c)) in det rho(I_F).
This value has order prime to p, and hence lies in omega(Teich(D)). Since n is a p-power and chi(C)
has order prime to p, the map z -> z^n permutes chi(C). Consequently
chi(C) is contained in omega(Teich(D)).
(1)
In particular every source phase has order dividing Q. This conclusion does not require selecting a
splitting of the tame quotient or choosing Frobenius representatives.
Choose an integer k_0 with n k_0 congruent to1 modulo Q. When Q=1 take k_0=1. Define
delta(u)=omega(Teich(u))^(k_0),
u in D.
Because exponentiation by k_0 is an automorphism on every group of roots of unity of order dividing
Q, delta(D)=omega(Teich(D)). Define the finite fiber product
C_tilde={(c,u) in C times D : chi(c)=delta(u)}.
(2)
It is a subgroup, and projection pr:C_tilde -> C is surjective by (1). Define the actual central matrix
homomorphism
g(c,u)=Teich(u^(k_0)) I_n.
(3)
Its action on Lambda and Pi is the central-character scalar
Lambda(g(c,u))=omega(Teich(u^(k_0)))I
=delta(u)I=chi(c)I.
(4)
If (1,u) belongs to ker pr, (4) is the identity. Hence the represented action factors uniquely through
C. It is exactly the prescribed source action. Although selecting a particular matrix representative for
c may require a choice of u, the represented operator is independent of that choice. Changing k_0 by a
multiple of Q leaves (3) unchanged.
All matrices (3) are central. Their conjugation on actual groups, characters, and scalar pushouts is
therefore the identity, and their Lambda operators are scalar. Thus they preserve every e and every
sector E. The source extension action is also the identity by hypothesis, so any attachment of those
scalar extensions is equivariant. Both honest carrier actions are chi(c)I, so every Heisenberg intertwiner
intertwines C without a new phase choice.
For the recovery step, put P={a in N:Lambda(a)eLambda(a)^(-1)=e}. Then F× is contained in P. The
retained maps
Phi:Ind_P^N E -> Lambda,
j:Lambda -> Ind_P^N E
are N-equivariant. They therefore commute with all actual matrices (3), and ker pr also acts trivially
on Ind_P^N E: its matrices are central elements of P acting trivially on E, hence trivially on every
induced translate. Thus the equality descends through pr to C. The recovering idempotent, and then
compact induction to GL_n(F), preserve this equivariance. They recover the same fixed Lambda and

E.3 3. What this closes and what it does not
For a source packet whose marked tensor carrier is the entire rank-n source, this proves the stabilizer
step whenever its genuine tame operators are scalar and an actual host with the correct central character
and full-character attachment is already present. There is no remaining scalar-phase equation to solve
in that situation: the determinant and central character supply it.
If only the source symplectic C action is known to be trivial, the preceding STABILIZER_CONTRAC
T166.md proves triviality of its full scalar-extension action for prime-to-p C. Schur then gives a scalar
packet character. To apply the present theorem one must still identify that character with the action of
actual inertia on the full source. That identification holds when the supplied honest packet carrier is
the whole source carrier. It is not automatic for a proper multiplicity-space factor, whose omitted factor
can contribute to the determinant.
For several factors the total packet character is the product of the supplied factor characters. The
theorem matches that product on the whole attached packet. It does not represent independent factor
actions by distinct central matrices unless those additional marked actions are separately specified and
verified.
The result uses the fixed full inducing representation Lambda. If Lambda|J=kappa_can tensor sigma,
then kappa_can and sigma are both unchanged. Equation(4) concerns Lambda, and does not assert
that kappa_can alone has the same scalar character. A contract prescribing an action specifically on the
canonical beta extension requires that distinction to remain explicit.
No nontrivial source symplectic action is realized here. No new base candidate, new H5 comparison,
dyadic quadratic refinement, or general rank theorem is claimed. Existing quadratic refinements are
preserved because the actual central conjugation action is the identity.
E.4 4. Why a direct map C into residue units is too strong
Take q=5, n=5^r, and let omega on k×=F5× be the quadratic character. Let C=C2 and let chi be its

character1. Consequently
omega(a(c)) = chi(c)^n
is impossible at the nontrivial c, since n is odd. The proposed direct section is not forced by genuine

J.7 7. Which repairs have actually been tested
J.7.1 Replacing the displayed type or parameter at fixed Swan and torsion
At ranks2 and4 this fails by Sections4–5 for every maximal simple type satisfying those invariants.
A new matrix search or a different critical coefficient cannot manufacture the missing quotient
dimensions.
At rank8 the full tower supplies the good profile, but the three invariants alone do not force it inside
a separately selected candidate. Section6 proves the failure of that proposed inference with an explicit
actual host. A finer endo-class or ramification comparison would be needed for that same-candidate
assertion.
J.7.2 Skipping approximation degrees or changing critical parity
At rank2 there is no degree to skip. At rank4 the level excludes both a scalar minimal approximation
and a full-degree minimal approximation. The remaining quadratic derived step has odd critical
exponent by minimality. Thus neither skipping nor declaring that exponent even is a valid repair at
fixed invariants.
At rank8 a degree skip is genuinely possible, but it decreases capacity in the explicit example above.
J.7.3 Scalar twists, shallow or deep
A scalar twist of the existing actual inducing representation does not increase its dimension. The
exact Block164 pushout transport identifies the same quotient J/H and leaves its commutator pairing
unchanged. Thus it cannot turn an insufficient eta into a whole source carrier.
For an actual parameter, replacing beta by beta+aI with a∈F leaves its field, centralizer and
commutator map unchanged. A shallow scalar addition does not change the leading level. A
dominating scalar addition can change that level, but it contributes no new noncentral Heisenberg
directions: in the defining sequence the added scalar stage has equal H and J orders. This agrees with
the exact representation-level twist transport. Enlarging a displayed numerical level is therefore not a
capacity repair.
This paragraph does not assert that every arbitrary scalar character twist is represented by one
globally specified additive parameter. The already proved group/representation transport suffices for
its negative capacity conclusion.
J.7.4 Adding residue multiplicity or increasing ambient rank
The torsion-one condition forces a full-degree totally ramified parameter field and residue multiplicity
one. A host with an unramified or residual multiplicity factor does not preserve that invariant.
Increasing the ambient rank changes the required source rank. Neither maneuver closes the current
fixed-rank construction.
J.7.5 Using a larger arithmetic carrier inside the same representation
A larger compact subgroup representation, a genuinely different arithmetic quotient, or an
induction-stage carrier might have enough dimension. Such an enlargement is not ruled out
here. It would need an actual finite Heisenberg action carrying the prescribed full source data and a
proved recovery in the unchanged candidate. Artificially adding vector-space copies or transporting
abstract operators to an induced space does not provide that arithmetic attachment or prove its kernel
compatibility. No such repair is constructed in this note.
J.8 8. Quadratic refinements and marked centers
For d>=3, the dimension result gives a symplectic embedding of the source quotient into the actual host
quotient. With C trivial, a C×-central pushout can then be matched by its alternating commutator, and
Stone–von Neumann supplies the corresponding source sector. This is the same finite scalar-pushout
attachment contract used previously.
At p=2, that statement must not be promoted to an identification of arbitrary preselected native
quadratic refinements. The C× pushout permits rescaling lifts by i and can identify the pushouts of
the dihedral and quaternion extraspecial planes, even though their native square functions differ. A
chosen source embedding can preserve that source’s full finite central extension and its character values.
It does not thereby identify a separately marked target mu_2 extension or its Arf invariant.
In particular, symplectic-isotropic reduction respects a prescribed quadratic form only when the
reduced subspace is totally singular for that form. The retained DYADIC_AND_WEAK_ATTACHMENT159.md
gives the exact quadratic/Arf obstruction. Additional source or target marked centers, chosen lifts,
quadratic refinements and nontrivial stabilizer actions therefore require their own comparison. They
are neither erased from the task nor supplied by a dimension inequality.
J.9 9. Scope and source provenance
The strongest proved conclusion is exact capacity for the specified actual full defining profile, together
with invariant low-rank failures and an explicit rank-eight counterexample to numerical profile forcing.
No universal impossibility for original Theorem16.2 is asserted. In particular this note supplies no
complete original H1–H5 counterexample and does not decide whether that endpoint requires this
precise whole-maximal-type-carrier realization.

b_i²=t_i,
[a_i,a_j]=c_ij, [b_i,b_j]=d_ij.
Every element has a unique normal form
z a_1^(epsilon_1) ... a_m^(epsilon_m), epsilon_i in {0,1},
and analogously on the target. The multiplication is completely determined by the displayed squares
and commutators.

c_ij=d_ij for every i,j,
s_i/t_i belongs to Z² for every i.
(1)

ABSTRACT. Let ¯ρ be a residual Galois representation and let R be a global deformation ring with declared
local conditions. We separate the global automorphy problem into residual occupancy, deformation
support, Hecke occupancy, and arithmetic realization. Local conditions are encoded by quotient rings
rather than by idempotents, since irreducible components of a local deformation ring need not be clopen.
For an ordinary or derived patching datum, full support descends through the augmentation quotient.
Near faithfulness is shown to be equivalent to full support for finite modules over Noetherian rings. An
isomorphism R ∼= T transports support, Fitting ideals, and point fibers, but a quotient map can erase
an entire component. Finite Hecke algebras are resolved into canonical Artin packets, so simultaneous
generalized eigenspaces are available without assuming semisimplicity. Nested packets in one finite carrier
stabilize; for changing finite carriers, nonzero stable cores give compatible inverse limit vectors. These
results give a pointwise criterion: a characteristic zero deformation point in automorphic support produces
a Hecke eigensystem. With attached Galois representations, local global compatibility, and classicality, the
point is automorphic. A fixed compatible system then propagates the conclusion to every coefficient place.
For finite coefficient quotients, compatible conjugacy classes admit compatible continuous representatives.
Declared polynomial quotient conditions survive their adic reconstruction. These completion statements
require explicit finite occupancy, continuity, and integral Frobenius data. Universal companion existence
and unrestricted reciprocity are not proved.

1 Introduction
Automorphy lifting joins several kinds of mathematics that are easy to conflate. A residual
representation must first occur in an automorphic carrier. The chosen characteristic zero representation
must lie on a deformation problem controlled by local conditions. A patching argument must show
that the automorphic module reaches the relevant part of the deformation space. A comparison such as
R ∼= T must identify the arithmetic and Hecke coordinates. Finally, the resulting Hecke point must be
classical and must carry the expected Galois representation with the required local compatibility.
None of these steps is merely a change of notation. A deeper lift above one residual representation
cannot create a missing residual companion. Freeness over an auxiliary group algebra does not imply
that every component of a deformation ring is occupied. An isomorphism of rings transports support
that already exists, but it does not create a nonzero automorphic vector. A nonzero class in completed
or torsion cohomology need not be classical without a theorem that says so.

The Taylor Wiles method and its later forms solve these problems in many important settings
[27, 24, 9, 14, 12]. Higher dimensional and derived versions use a broader range of local deformation
rings, residual image conditions, torsion classes, and cohomological carriers [8, 3, 6, 25, 17, 22, 7, 19].
The present article does not replace those theorems. It isolates the algebraic support statements that
explain exactly what a patching package supplies once its arithmetic hypotheses have been verified.
The first correction concerns local packets. A local deformation ring is usually complete and local. Its
irreducible components are rarely open and closed. They cannot generally be represented by central
idempotents. The correct object is a quotient ring defining a local condition, together with the support
of a module or complex on the resulting spectrum. Central idempotents reappear later, where they
belong, inside finite Artin Hecke algebras and finite dimensional characteristic zero carriers.
The second correction concerns patching. The useful global conclusion is full support, often expressed
as near faithfulness. For a finite module over a Noetherian ring, near faithfulness is equivalent to
full support. Full support descends through the quotient that removes the auxiliary variables. This
statement is elementary, but it is the exact bridge from a patched module to componentwise occupancy
at finite level. The same conclusion holds for perfect complexes through derived support.
The third correction concerns Hecke packets. Semisimplicity is not required to isolate a maximal
Hecke packet. Every finite commutative algebra over a field is a product of Artin local algebras. Its
canonical central idempotents project onto simultaneous generalized eigenspaces. Trace is only a
secondary criterion in characteristic zero. Support and localization are the primary notions.
The last part assembles these statements into a conditional theorem. A characteristic zero point of R
is automorphic when it lies in the support of the automorphic carrier, the comparison with the Hecke
algebra is available, and the corresponding Hecke fiber satisfies the declared realization theorem. If
the point belongs to a fixed strictly compatible system, equality of Frobenius polynomials propagates
the automorphic identification to every coefficient place by Chebotarev density and Brauer Nesbitt
[5, 18, 12].
The organization is as follows. Local quotient conditions are developed in section 3. Adequacy and
residual occupancy appear in section 4. Auxiliary group algebras are treated in section 5. Ordinary and
derived patching support appear in section 6. The effect of R ∼= T is isolated in section 7. Finite Hecke
packets and infinite occupancy are developed in section 8. Pointwise automorphy and compatible
systems appear in sections 9 and 10. The coefficient prime two is discussed in section 11. The final
conditional theorem is stated in section 12.
